Biscuit Basin in Yellowstone National Park/ Shutterstock Image Home Idaho Yellowstone What state is Yellowstone National Park in? What state is Yellowstone National Park in? Key Takeaways: Yellowstone spans **Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho**—but 96% lies in Wyoming, so plan logistics accordingly. All five park entrances are open 24/7 year‑round, though some may close temporarily due to weather—check before arriving. Cell service is limited; download maps and the Shaka Guide app ahead of time, and pack essentials like water, snacks, and layers. Introduction Yellowstone National Park is renowned for its stunning geothermal wonders, diverse wildlife, and pristine natural landscapes. The greater Yellowstone area spans across three states, including south-central Montana, eastern Idaho, and northeast Wyoming. What state contains most of Yellowstone? Yellowstone National Park is primarily situated in the state of Wyoming, which holds 96% of the park's land area. How big is Yellowstone National Park? Yellowstone National Park is vast, covering a sprawling 2.2 million acres. It is the 8th largest national park in the United States and offers a wide variety of environments to explore, including mountains, meadows, canyons, rivers, hills, and valleys. Entrances of Yellowstone National Park Yellowstone boasts five entrances that allow visitors to access the park from different directions, each offering its own unique attractions. West Entrance-West Yellowstone, Wyoming The West Entrance is located by the lively town of West Yellowstone and is by far the most popular entrance. South Entrance-Jackson, Wyoming The South Entrance is just above Grand Teton National Park, and Jackson Wyoming offers lots of upscale accommodations for those interested in a luxe stay. East Entrance-Cody, Wyoming The East Entrance is one of the more remote entrances to Yellowstone, but beyond Yellowstone Lake and the Absaroka Mountains lies one of the largest cities nearest Yellowstone. The city of Cody is famous for its Western heritage and the Buffalo Bill Center of the West. Northeast Entrance-Cooke City, Montana The Northeast Entrance is just beyond the famous wildlife hotspot, Lamar Valley. Cooke City is one of the smaller entrance towns but offers accommodations, restaurants, and gear rentals. North Entrance-Gardiner, Montana The North Entrance is Yellowstone’s most iconic entrance, with the historic Roosevelt Arch welcoming visitors to their park journey. The North Entrance Road was re-routed following the unprecedented flooding of 2022, but the new road offers some spectacular views of Mammoth Hot Springs. Activities in Yellowstone National Park Shutterstock Image Yellowstone offers a wide range of activities for visitors to enjoy, including: Wildlife Viewing: Observe bison, elk, wolves, bears, and more in their natural habitats. Hiking: Explore numerous trails, from easy walks to challenging backcountry routes. Geothermal Features: Witness geysers, hot springs, and mud pots, including big names such as Old Faithful Geyser. Fishing: The park's rivers and lakes are great for anglers. Camping: Stay in campgrounds or backcountry sites to immerse yourself in the park's wilderness. Photography: Capture the park's breathtaking landscapes, wildlife, and geothermal features. The unique and vibrant scenery makes it a paradise for photographers. Boating: Explore the park's lakes, including Yellowstone Lake, by kayak, canoe, or motorized boat. It's an excellent way to enjoy the pristine waters and surrounding views. Biking: There’s nothing quite like exploring the roads and trails of Yellowstone with your own two legs. E-bike rentals are available locally for those looking to explore more with less time. Ranger Programs: Join ranger-led programs and educational talks to gain insights into the park's history, geology, and wildlife. Is Yellowstone National Park open year-round? Shutterstock Image Yes — Yellowstone National Park is open year-round, but accessibility changes with the seasons. While the park itself never closes, many roads and facilities shut down in winter, so your experience depends on when you visit. Spring: Snowmelt can cause flooding, and some roads may remain closed. Summer: All major roads and facilities are open, though heavy crowds make parking difficult. Fall: Visitor numbers drop, but many facilities begin closing in late September and early October. Winter: Most park roads close to regular traffic, but guided snowmobile and snowcoach tours are available. How many people visit Yellowstone in a year? Shutterstock Image Yellowstone National Park welcomes around 4 million visitors annually. The best time to visit depends on your preferences. Summer is the busiest, offering pleasant weather and full accessibility. However, for a quieter experience, consider visiting in spring or fall when the crowds diminish, and wildlife is more active. Since then, she’s explored national parks across the country, learning the history, ecology, and culture that shape these wild places.
